items.title: $40M bridge eases traffic and delivers other benefits to Mississauga: councillor
items.summary: Residents, businesses and, most directly, motorists have reaped the benefits since a new bridge built over a busy railway line in Mississauga’s north end opened to traffic nearly one year ago, city officials say. The long-awaited $40-million Goreway Drive Overpass above the CN train tracks in Malton, near Toronto Pearson Airport, has eased gridlock that previously plagued the corridor for decades as motorists travelled between Mississauga and Brampton. The four-lane overpass, also referred to as the Goreway Bridge, took its first vehicles last Oct. 15. ” This week, City of Mississauga Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart confirmed the overpass has indeed delivered the goods not only for daily traffic, but also for residents and businesses in her ward. com the overpass is “incredibly important” to the community in several ways. “It has improved traffic flow along Goreway (Drive), but also the other north/south arterials,” she said. “Most notably, we no longer see vehicle traffic stuck at the tracks for the train traffic that is moving goods in our community. This is good for business and residents alike.

items.title: Great Outdoors Comedy Festival Postpones Mississauga Event With John Mulaney
items.summary: The three-day festival was set to debut at Erindale Park this weekend, but organizers have postponed the event without explaining why.

items.title: Discovering the Trans Canada Trail in Mississauga
items.summary: Presented in partnership with the Trans Canada Trail. I’ve lived in Mississauga since August of 1994 and have experienced nearly every part of the city from Meadowvale to Port Credit. ) This year, I decided to dedicate a day to exploring Mississauga’s contribution to the trail through four different locations, all conveniently located on the shores of Lake Ontario. For all the travel that I’ve done in my 15+ year career, I was excited to adventure in my back yard. For reference, the TCT is nearly 30,000 kilometres long and this is my second official experience this year, with the first being in Quebec’s P’tit Train du Nord. THE 2027 SUBARU TRAILSEEKER ELECTRIC VEHICLE AT LAKEFRONT PROMENADE PARK. As I’ve also reviewed new cars for the past 15 years via Modern Motoring, I decided to use an electric vehicle, the 2027 Subaru Trailseeker, as my car for this adventure. In this article, I’ll walk you through the four parts of the trail I did, all of which are accessible and approachable for all ages and capabilities. Whether it’s a short or long voyage by foot or by two wheels, the TCT is a wonderful, free resource that’s available to everyone. On the east side of Mississauga in Lakeview is Lakefront Promenade Park, featuring boat launches, a beach and excellent views of Lake Ontario. It’s also part of Mississauga’s extensive Waterfront Trail. There’s plenty of free parking and you’ll see walkers, joggers, runners and cyclists enjoy this part of the TCT. There’s a boardwalk and wildlife to enjoy, while the balance of the trail is paved for heightened accessibility. Bring your own food and or drink to enjoy along the trail and you can launch your kayak, canoe or standup paddle board.

items.title: Pearson Airport's Terminal Overhaul Comes With More Than 30 New Places to Eat and Shop
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto Pearson Airport is adding more than 30 new retail, dining and lounge locations across its terminals as part of what officials are calling a landmark commercial expansion. The outlet reports the new businesses, opening throughout 2026, mix Canadian-owned and Toronto-founded brands with internationally recognized names. INsauga reports Toronto Pearson CEO Deborah Flint said in a news release that for millions of travellers each year, the airport is where journeys begin, connections are made and Canada comes to life. According to the outlet, the commercial rollout comes as Canada's busiest airport moves ahead with one of the largest airport infrastructure projects in the country's history. INsauga reports the Greater Toronto Airports Authority's Pearson LIFT program, short for Long-term Investment in Facilities and Terminals, has been in development for years and aims to modernize and expand the airport over the next decade. According to the outlet, contracts for the terminal modernization project were awarded in July.

items.title: City Renews 'Stoop and Scoop' Push as Dog Waste Complaints Keep Piling Up in Mississauga Parks
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga officials say the problem of dog owners failing to clean up after their pets in public spaces has continued despite years of effort to curb it. The outlet reports the city has struggled to enforce the bylaw covering improper disposal of dog waste, which carries fines ranging from $115 to $180, and has instead leaned on public education campaigns urging owners to stoop and scoop. INsauga reports the city said in a Wednesday social media post that dog waste is still causing quite a stink in Mississauga, pointing to messes turning up in parks and other public areas. According to the outlet, officials are asking residents to use a different bin if one is full, or to take a filled bag home, and to report overflowing bins to 311. INsauga reports the city said dog waste belongs in garbage bins or at designated dog waste stations, which are located throughout Mississauga and are meant to make disposal safer and reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Peel Police Recover $15,000 in Stolen Goods After Retail Theft Probe Leads to Brampton Search
items.summary: According to INsauga, four Brampton residents are facing numerous charges following a Peel Regional Police investigation into a string of organized retail thefts across the Greater Toronto Area. The outlet reports the probe began in Mississauga after officers responded to a reported theft at a business near Clayhill Road and Dundas Street West on June 18. INsauga reports investigators with the 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau identified several suspects and linked them to additional thefts throughout Peel Region. According to the outlet, police executed a search warrant on July 20 at a residence near Mississauga Road and Mayfield Road in Brampton, recovering roughly $15,000 worth of property stolen from fitness, department and pharmacy stores. INsauga reports the recovered items included electronics, health and fitness products, household goods, supplements and cosmetics, along with two seized vehicles, jewelry and cash in various currencies. According to the outlet, 43-year-old Czuljana Ciecierska is among those charged, facing seven counts of theft under $5,000, one count of theft over $5,000, and charges of possessing and laundering proceeds of crime.

items.title: Mississauga Staff Say Province's Data Centre Rules Leave Cities Unable to Enforce Community Perks
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city planning staff say Ontario's new framework for regulating data centres would leave municipalities without the legal tools to hold developers to promises like funding parks and community centres. The outlet reports a staff report heading to general committee recommends council formally respond to the province's draft Data Centre Playbook before its public comment period closes September 12. Mississauga.com reports the report arrives six weeks after council voted unanimously on July 29 to direct staff to draft a bylaw pausing new major data centre applications for a year, a move that would make Mississauga the first GTA municipality to do so if council approves it at a final vote September 16. According to the outlet, that push followed opposition to a proposed Prologis data centre in Meadowvale Business Park, where more than 20 residents raised concerns at the July 29 meeting about noise, energy demand and proximity to homes. Mississauga.com reports the provincial framework, released August 13, outlines how data centre proposals seeking to connect to Ontario's electricity grid will be evaluated. According to the outlet, city staff say they broadly support the province's effort to regulate the sector but the report identifies a fundamental disconnect in how the Playbook is written.

items.title: Mississauga Drivers Get Double the Time to Fight Parking Tickets as City Adopts Plate-Reading Cameras
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga will begin using Licence Plate Recognition technology starting in October to issue parking tickets, automatically photographing plates on illegally parked vehicles before mailing tickets to registered owners. The outlet reports the city said the new process supports parking enforcement officers in places where issuing a physical penalty notice may not be effective, such as school zones and time-limited parking zones. INsauga reports the technology is meant to improve safety for enforcement officers while enhancing how the city delivers parking services. According to the outlet, the launch is one of several changes coming to Mississauga's parking enforcement division in October. INsauga reports drivers who are ticketed will now have 30 days to pay the fine or request a review of the penalty, double the current 15-day window. According to the outlet, the changes were approved by city council in July as part of a broader effort to modernize parking enforcement, improve compliance and enhance service delivery efficiency.

items.title: Every One of Mississauga's Cheapest August Home Sales Was a Condo, Zoocasa Finds
items.summary: According to INsauga, the least expensive home sold in Mississauga last month went for $309,000, according to a Zoocasa analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The outlet reports every one of the least expensive homes sold in August was a condo apartment. INsauga reports the average price for a condo apartment in Mississauga fell to $495,052 in August, down from $511,649 in July and from $549,936 in August 2025. According to the outlet, one of the least expensive sales was a three-bedroom, two-storey condo in Sheridan near the QEW and Clarkson GO Station, which sold for $400,000, above its $384,900 list price. INsauga reports another was an updated one-bedroom condo in City Centre featuring floor-to-ceiling windows, stainless steel appliances and a parking space with a locker.

items.title: Mulaney Says Festival's Postponement Wasn't His Call, Plans Return to the Region Soon
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, comedian John Mulaney says he intends to perform in the Mississauga region soon after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival he was set to headline was postponed at the last minute. The outlet reports the festival, scheduled to run at Erindale Park from Friday to Sunday, was called off in an Instagram post from organizers on Tuesday. According to the Star, organizers wrote that postponing the show was the right decision to ensure they could deliver the best possible festival, even though they knew there was a lot of excitement around it. The outlet reports Mulaney posted on social media Tuesday night saying the decision to move the festival's dates was not his. According to the Star, organizers are exploring new dates and plan to follow up directly with ticket holders.

items.title: Buffalo-area father loses legs, son faces multiple surgeries after Mississauga highway crash
items.summary: A father and son from the Buffalo area are battling life-altering injuries following a multi-vehicle crash in Mississauga last month. Masud Biswas, 43, has lost both of his legs above the knee, while his 12-year-old son, Marif, has undergone multiple surgeries and could face dozens more as doctors work to save his legs and help him regain the ability to walk. The Amherst, New York, family was returning home from Toronto on Aug. 11 when Masud and Marif were involved in a collision on Highway 403 in Mississauga. The extent of their injuries was not known when the crash was first reported. Ontario Provincial Police initially said the father and son had suffered critical, life-threatening injuries and were taken to trauma centres. ” According to a GoFundMe campaign established by neighbours of the family, Masud remains hospitalized in Ontario in stable condition following the amputations. Marif has undergone about half a dozen surgeries so far, according to the fundraising campaign. He has since been transferred to Golisano Children’s Hospital in Buffalo, where he is also in stable condition. Doctors are trying to save Marif’s legs, but he could require dozens more surgeries during what is expected to be a long recovery, the GoFundMe says. Before the crash, Marif was a seventh-grade student at Amherst Middle School who enjoyed playing soccer and basketball. While recovering in hospital, he has been keeping busy by building Lego sets.
